extracted.intended_audience: early career scientists seeking the Royal Society Dorothy Hodgkin Fellowship (applicants requiring flexible working patterns)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for applying to the Royal Society Dorothy Hodgkin Fellowship, a targeted eight-year award to support outstanding early-career scientists who need flexible working arrangements. Includes eligibility rules, permitted costs, assessment process, interview aims, and adjustments for disabled applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheme objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: The objectives of the DHF programme are to enable the next generation of research leaders to: Build an independent research career at a UK university or research institution; Gain the freedom, time and long-term flexible support to pursue high quality and innovative lines of scientific research; Develop as a research leader by offering tailored, high quality professional development, networking and engagement opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should frame their proposal and career plans to demonstrate how the fellowship will enable independence, provide time and flexibility for high-quality innovative research, and support leadership development. Case studies and the Career Pathway Tracker are provided as examples of impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship duration and mid-fellowship review
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships are for eight years, with years six to eight being subject to satisfactory progress demonstrated in a mid-fellowship review at year four.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful applicants should plan a research and career-development trajectory consistent with an eight-year fellowship and be prepared for a formal mid-fellowship review at year four that determines continuation into years six to eight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding cap and eligible costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants can apply for up to a maximum of ������������������������ 1.87 million over eight years. Funds can cover: Contribution to the award holder's salary; Indirect and estate costs; Equipment costs and research expenses including consumables, travel, etc.; Contribution towards research assistance salary and associated indirect and estate costs; Support for a new four-year PhD studentship(s); Relocation and visa costs for the applicants and their dependants (partner and children). The total grant cap may be exceeded in order to cover relocation/visa costs if this is well justified in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, justified budget lines for salary, indirect costs, equipment, research assistance, studentships and relocation/visa costs. Refer to the scheme notes and Royal Society Funding Guidance for full funding details. If claiming relocation/visa costs that exceed the cap, include strong justification in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility and provisions for personal circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: We provide flexibility to accommodate personal circumstances including part-time working for health reasons or caring responsibilities. There is provision for maternity, paternity, shared parental, adoptive or extended sick leave, as well as financial support for childcare costs that arise from attending conferences and research visits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When describing your working plan and commitments, explain any required flexible working pattern and how the fellowship will accommodate it. Applicants may request adjustments and should detail any leave plans or part-time arrangements and how these affect research delivery and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary eligibility: need for flexible support
rubrics_metrics.description: This scheme is for you if: You currently have, or will have by the start of the fellowship, a need for flexible support due to personal circumstances. This can include parental responsibilities, caring responsibilities, and/or clinically diagnosed health conditions that create a need for a flexible working pattern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must show a demonstrable need for flexible working support linked to personal circumstances; the Grants team will view this information to check eligibility. Explain clearly why flexible support is required and how it impacts your ability to pursue an independent research career.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary eligibility: early career stage (research experience limit)
rubrics_metrics.description: You are in the early stages of your research career having up to six years of research experience since your PhD by the closing date of the round; please refer to the scheme notes for further detail about the review of career breaks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculate and document research experience since PhD; if you have career breaks, consult the scheme notes for how they are taken into account. Ensure you meet the six-year limit (or have allowable adjustments) at the closing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary eligibility: employment status (no permanent post)
rubrics_metrics.description: You do not hold a permanent post (including proleptic appointment) in a university or not-for-profit organisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you hold or will hold a permanent or proleptic appointment at the fellowship start date, you are not eligible. Confirm employment status clearly in the application and check timing of any appointments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary eligibility: prior equivalent fellowships
rubrics_metrics.description: You do not hold, or have not previously held, an equivalent fellowship that provides an opportunity to establish an independent research group and therefore independent research status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have previously held a fellowship that conferred independent research status or opportunity to establish a group, you are ineligible. Disclose prior fellowships and their nature; consult scheme notes if in doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research remit eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Your research is within the Royal Society's remit of natural sciences, which includes but is not limited to biological research and biomedical sciences, chemistry, engineering, mathematics and physics. For a full list, please see the breakdown of subject groups and areas supported by the Royal Society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate clearly how your proposal fits within the Royal Society's natural sciences remit. Use the subject-group breakdown question (see below) and consult scheme notes if your field sits at an interface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nationality and visa eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants can be of any nationality and those requiring a visa are eligible to apply for a Global Talent Visa under the fast-track process of endorsement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International applicants may apply and should indicate visa/relocation needs. The scheme supports relocation and visa costs and applicants intending to apply for Global Talent endorsement should follow guidance and include necessary justification and budget lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application platform and preliminary steps
rubrics_metrics.description: You will apply through our application and grant management system, Flexi-Grant����. See the 'Application and assessment process' page for a general overview of the application and selection steps and below for details specific to this scheme. We recommend reading the information in full and contacting your host organisation Research Office in the first instance with any questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare your application in Flexi-Grant, ensure host organisation sign-off/timeframes are managed via Research Office, and read scheme notes in full before submission. Use provided downloads (scheme notes, conditions, FAQs, case studies) to inform application content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject categorisation question
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject categorisation �������������������������������� ��������������� a new question in the Research Proposal section of the form allows applicants to indicate whether their proposal is primarily in Biological Sciences or Physical Sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the appropriate primary subject area when completing the Research Proposal section; this helps categorise proposals for review and panel assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment process and confidentiality of flexibility information
rubrics_metrics.description: Your need for flexibility will only be viewed by the Society's Grants team to check your eligibility for the scheme. Following eligibility checks, applications are initially assessed by two panel members who have the most appropriate scientific expertise. A longlist is drawn up, with longlisted applications subject to independent peer review. Following completion of independent peer review, a shortlist for interview is drawn up with oversight from the Panel Chair. At the end of the interview stage, the Panel will confirm the recommendations for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect staged assessment: eligibility check (Grants team sees flexibility need), initial scientific assessment by two panel members, longlisting and independent peer review, shortlist and in-person interview, and final panel decision. Confidentiality of flexibility requests is maintained and not normally shared with panel members unless necessary (permission will be sought if sharing is required).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview aim and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: For the Dorothy Hodgkin Fellowship, shortlisted applicants will be invited to an in-person interview at the Royal Society. The aim of the interview is for you to demonstrate the importance and scientific validity of your work and for you to also describe how the award will lead to your scientific independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare to articulate the scientific importance and validity of your research and provide a clear narrative of how the fellowship will enable your transition to independent research leadership. Practical adjustments for interview attendance can be requested via the Grants team.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support and adjustments for disabled applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: The Royal Society welcomes applications from disabled scientists and provides support and adjustments to ensure that they can participate fully in the selection process. All requests for adjustments are made in confidentiality. Any request for an adjustment will not normally be shared with panel members unless it becomes relevant to the assessment process itself. If we need to share your request with anyone (for example if panel members are required to implement any adjustments during interviews), we will ask for your permission first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjustments can include, but are not limited to: Extension of the deadline; Additional support to complete the application form; Receiving the application form in a different format, such as on a Word document; Support during interviews as required, including technical support for candidates requiring accessibility software or services; Additional costs that candidates may incur on account of their particular disability to attend an interview. Contact the Grants team confidentially to request adjustments and provide supporting information as needed.
